races.name: CopyBet Follow Us On X Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
races.verdict: KING ROLY is back at the top of his game and went like the best horse at the weights when denied by a stablemate at Cartmel. He can land a second C&D success. Snipe has to be the danger after his near-miss at Warwick.

runners.note: Useful hurdler but below that level over fences. Didn't fire in 2 runs for new yard 6 months apart last season and his mark looks stiff now handicapping in this sphere back from a breathing operation.

Two hunter chase wins this year and also a creditable sixth in the Aintree Foxhunter in April. Better for comeback and just failed in 3-runner handicap at Warwick (25f) a fortnight ago. Got to be respected after that.

Back on track of late, resuming winning ways in C&D handicap in August in first-time blinkers. Foiled by a stablemate delivered later at Cartmel last time but went like the best horse at the weights and could be up to de

Won 3m Southwell handicap chase in March 2025. Didn't fire in 3 runs last season but returns off last successful mark for in-form yard and could go well.
On the up in 3m handicap hurdles when last seen in February 2025, winning at Wincanton and Taunton. Long absence to overcome but should make up into a chaser (has a pointing background).

races.verdict: Clive Cox has brought his juveniles on appreciably for a run this season so CASTLEROCK GIRL is fancied to go one better after her encouraging debut at Southwell 2 weeks ago. Form pick Californian Angel remains with potential so is the obvious threat.

races.name: CopyBet For Premier League Profit Boosts Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
races.verdict: KELIJOE would have made an impressive start over fences at Uttoxeter in March had he stood up (unseated 2 out when almost 20 lengths clear) and looks sure to win races in this sphere on that showing. This represents a classier field but he can make amends if ready to go. All 5 of his rivals could make their mark over fences, with Draco Malfoy perhaps the most interesting on his return.

runners.note: Successful over hurdles at Huntingdon (after 10 months off) and Hereford (2¾m) last season. Possesses the background/build to make a better chaser and first time up could be a good time to catch him.

£100,000 point winner (also fairly useful in bumpers) who was successful in 19f Catterick novice hurdle on New Year's Day. Should have a good future over fences (top yard 5-11 with chase debutants this season).
Made a good start over hurdles and placed 3 times at up to 2½m last season. Bred to have a future over fences.

Successful over hurdles as a 4-y-o and fair runs when twice completing last season (beaten 9 lengths in second in 4-runner 2¾m Fontwell handicap in February). Needs to improve now chasing on his return but no surprise if

Fair in bumpers and matched that level sent handicapping over hurdles when landing a gamble in 13-runner event at Taunton (19f) in January. Good efforts next 2 starts and should make his mark over fences.

Fairly useful French bumper winner who took a Doncaster novice handicap hurdle last December and was in the process of demolishing his rivals on chasing debut at Uttoxeter (2½m) in March when rather unfortunate to depart

Sent off 33/1 and merely matched debut form when eighth of 14 in maiden at Leopardstown (7f, good to firm) 48 days ago.
Tenth of 15 in maiden at Naas (7f, good to soft, 300/1) 20 days ago and drop in trip looks against him.
Cheap purchase who was sent off 150/1 when seventh of 12 in maiden at Gowran (1m, soft) on debut 18 days ago. Gelded after, and down in trip now, which won't help his cause.

Eleventh of 12 in maiden at Dundalk (6f, 200/1) 19 days ago.

Bred to be sharp and showed something to work on when seventh of 10 in maiden claimer at Naas (1m, good to soft) on debut 20 days ago, unable to sustain effort. Drop in trip therefore looks a good move.
Stuck to her task well when fifth of 13 in maiden on C&D debut 32 days ago, never nearer. Open to progress.
Foaled March 30. Inns of Court filly. Dam lightly raced out of US 6f winner Princess Janie.

races.name: Mowden Park RFC Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
races.verdict: Bumper winner ARMS PARK can make a successful start in this sphere with doubts surrounding chief threats Military Cross and John Galt.

races.verdict: NOWSHESDANCING is likely to be suited by this step up in trip so she gets the vote in a tight-looking handicap. Reem Rak is next best back on better ground, with handicap newcomer Palomezcal completing the shortlist.

Dundee Law has transferred to the Skeltons and could well have more to offer in the bumper sphere, while Royalty Row'd and winning pointer Lower De Couely are others to consider.

races.verdict: MY CUBBY BEAR returned to form when second in a 6f handicap at Cork last week and may well be up to going one better back in maiden company, especially if the standard-setter Almeiyda underperforms once again. Lilli's Angel has a progressive profile which must count for something in an ordinary race, while Port Arthur is another who merits consideration.

runners.note: Remains with just one standout effort, though was left poorly placed when down the field in 21-runner handicap here (5f) latest.
Second of 8 in barrier trial at Naas and showed some promise in a pair of 6f Curragh maidens 10 months apart. Underperformed at Cork when last seen in May but may bounce back after a break.
Sent off 150/1 in a hood for belated debut but showed some ability when third of 7 in maiden at Bellewstown (5f, soft) on debut last week. Longer trip likely to suit.
Well beaten in a trio of maidens, including in first-time blinkers last time.
Has an excellent pedigree but has made a most discouraging start to his career.

Improved again when fourth of 16 in maiden (12/1) at Cork (6f, good to soft) 38 days ago, faring best of those held up. Needs more again but that's feasible given the way her form is heading.

races.name: Fairlight Studios At Sedgefield Racecourse Handicap Chase
races.verdict: A good opportunity for FLASHY BOY to get back on track back down in class. Henry Box Brown can follow him home.

races.verdict: In receipt of her 5 lb sex allowance and following on from a promising debut at Newmarket, GAINFUL should take some stopping. That said, Top Scholar and Prince Of Petra are both bred to be well above average so need close attention in the market.

Maiden who has made little impact in nurseries. Races from 3 lb out of the weights.

races.verdict: JET OF DREAMS can confirm placings with Lady Kara with a competent claimer off-setting his penalty.

Asadjumeirah looks the main danger on recent form, though it's been a while since he's tackled turf, with Golden Prosperity taken to round out the 1-2-3.

races.name: Racing Again 21st October Handicap (0-60) (Div 2)
races.verdict: PURE GRANITE is lightly raced for his age and made more impact when fourth at Punchestown on his return from 10 months off. Entitled to strip fitter, he can build on that and open his account. Pebble Island rates the main danger if reproducing the form of his Fairyhouse second in June, while Patrick Street and Charlie Brow'n are also respected.

Lightly-raced maiden who shaped very well on handicap debut at Galway in July. Hasn't kicked on in 2 subsequent efforts.
Had been brought along with handicaps in mind in 1m/9f maidens but didn't get home upped to 1½m at Listowel on handicap bow. Should have more to offer now back at a more suitable trip.
Maiden who posted several solid in-frame efforts in spring/early-summer but arrives on the back of 2 poor efforts and may have gone off the boil for the time being.

races.verdict: ALPINARA looked a useful prospect when beating a couple of subsequent winners at Doncaster back in June so she looks the one to beat under a penalty. Yamnah was a big eyecatcher first-time out at Windsor and can offer most resistance.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Smartview Racecards Handicap
races.verdict: Not as competitive as the numbers suggest and ROYAL COUNTY GLORY is well worth forgiving a lesser effort on turf at Brighton and taken to bounce back in style returned to polytrack with Oisin Murphy in the saddle. Seeing Stars also goes well here and this C&D winner rates the chief threat ahead of Cixi and Upsomdowns.

races.verdict: An open sprint in which it could pay to side with KINIRO to bounce back in style off a lenient-looking mark now Oisin Murphy is back in the saddle. Madman is progressing well and rates a big threat though, while polytrack debutants Charlie Boyo and Blue Orbit command respect too.

races.name: Set Your Limits With Unibet Handicap
races.verdict: A few with chances but this could go the way of C&D scorer NOW THE EAGLE who wasn't seen to ideal effect when fourth at Newmarket last time and returns here on a lenient-looking mark. Hat-trick seeking Last Flight rates a big threat, while Luan is also well in the mix on the back of a facile Wolverhampton success.

runners.note: Kickstarted 2026 with success at Chelmsford in January but below par in 4 runs since, off 4 months before last of 8 in handicap at Newbury (1¼m, good to firm) 19 days ago. Significantly back up in trip.

Successful 3 times over hurdles for this yard, most recently in December. First Flat start since 2024 (tongue tied) when a good second of 7 in handicap at Lingfield (2m, all-weather) in August. Not out of things.
Won twice on the turf course (1m5f/2m) at Lingfield last summer. Only twice raced this season and off since being pulled up over C&D in May. Has something to prove.

A dual all-weather winner for James Ferguson in the summer. Easily off the mark for his new yard in 7-runner handicap at Wolverhampton (1½m) 19 days ago. Not taken lightly despite a 7 lb weights hike.

On the up for her new yard and landed 2m handicaps at Ffos Las in August and Southwell 15 days ago. Up another 4 lb but very much one to consider in her hat-trick bid.

races.name: Unibet 3 Uniboosts A Day Handicap
races.verdict: VIOLET GOLDSMITH rates the pick of the weights and with this return to 1m a positive she is fancied to resume winning ways. Mbappe hasn't been at his best this summer but Billy Loughnane takes the ride for the first time since his C&D success in the winter so merits consideration, especially if the market vibes are positive. Hat-trick seeking Snooker McCrew can also have a say.
